rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the highest-priority uncertainty is establishing a reliable performance floor. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible configuration: a single modality, a single profile (no aggregation complexity), and a deterministic linear encoder (PCA) with no training instability risk. This gives a clean, interpretable baseline accuracy against which all subsequent experiments—alternative RNA encoders, image modality, multiprofile aggregation, and multimodal fusion—can be compared. Choosing the simplest baseline first avoids confounding multiple design choices and ensures that any later improvement is attributable to a specific added component. It is the most uncertainty-reducing use of experiment 1 under a 10-experiment budget.

The only completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) yielded a low accuracy of 0.485, barely above chance, indicating the task is difficult and the current RNA representation may be insufficient. The single most important uncertainty is whether the image modality carries discriminative signal at all. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) isolates the image contribution using the simplest comparable setup (singleprofile, no aggregation), directly mirroring the baseline's simplicity. If image accuracy is substantially higher than 0.485, it validates investing remaining budget in multimodal fusion; if it is similarly low, it suggests focusing on RNA encoder improvements (scvi, scgpt) and multiprofile strategies. This single experiment reduces the most critical uncertainty about which modality to prioritize across the remaining 8 experiments.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved 0.485 accuracy, while config_010 (image_only, resnet50) was very weak at 0.208, indicating RNA is the dominant signal. However, we have only tested one RNA encoder (PCA, a linear method). Question: Does a learned nonlinear representation (scvi_n200) substantially outperform PCA for the RNA modality? This experiment changes only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while keeping singleprofile and rna_only fixed, directly isolating the encoder effect against config_001. Why now: With 7 experiments remaining, establishing whether the RNA representation is a bottleneck is the highest-leverage uncertainty to resolve. If scvi_n200 significantly improves accuracy, it justifies investing remaining budget in scvi-based multimodal configs; if it does not, PCA is sufficient and we can pivot to profile-setting or fusion experiments without wasting budget on scvi/scgpt variants.

Evidence: scvi_n200 (0.5203) clearly outperforms pca_n2000 (0.4849) as an RNA encoder in singleprofile rna_only settings, and image-only is very weak (0.2079). The major unexplored axis is whether multiprofile aggregation can further improve on the best singleprofile result. This experiment tests scvi_n200 with multiprofile + avgpool, isolating the effect of profile aggregation while holding the best-known encoder constant. Choosing avgpool over transformer keeps the comparison clean and avoids compounding two new variables (multiprofile + complex aggregation). If multiprofile+avgpool lifts accuracy above 0.52, it opens a promising direction for the remaining 6 experiments; if not, it confirms singleprofile is sufficient and we can pivot to testing scgpt or multimodal fusion with the best encoder. This is the highest-information experiment for reducing uncertainty about a core design axis with 6 experiments still remaining.

The strongest evidence so far shows that rna_only + scvi_n200 + multiprofile + avgpool (config_005, acc=0.650) dramatically outperforms all other tested configurations, with the multiprofile+avgpool combination contributing a +0.130 accuracy gain over singleprofile. The key remaining uncertainty within this promising direction is whether transformer aggregation can further improve over the simple avgpool. config_006 is a clean single-variable comparison (avgpool → transformer, all else identical: rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200), isolating the aggregation effect. This is the best use of experiment 5 because it directly exploits the strongest evidence, reduces uncertainty about the optimal aggregation for our best configuration, and the result will inform whether to build multimodal extensions on top of transformer or avgpool in the remaining 5 experiments.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 acc. Image-only with resnet50 is very weak (0.208), raising the question of whether image features add any complementary signal when fused with the strong RNA representation. Question: This experiment tests whether multimodal fusion (concat) of the best-known RNA pipeline (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) with resnet50 image features can exceed the 0.653 RNA-only baseline. It isolates the effect of adding the image modality while keeping all other RNA-side settings at their best-known values. Why this is the best use: With only 4 experiments remaining, we must determine early whether the multimodal direction is viable. If config_032 fails to beat 0.653, we can confidently allocate remaining budget to RNA-only improvements (e.g., scgpt encoder, config_009). If it succeeds, it opens a productive new direction. Testing this now avoids wasting late-budget experiments on a dead-end multimodal path.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688 acc. The most direct single-variable exploitation is to swap concat for weighted fusion (config_033), isolating the effect of fusion strategy while holding all other components constant. This is the cheapest possible test to determine whether the current best can be improved by a more expressive fusion mechanism. If weighted fusion yields a gain, it establishes a new best and confirms fusion as a key lever; if not, it confirms concat is optimal and the remaining 3 experiments can pivot to testing the image encoder (ViT-L) or RNA encoder (scGPT) as the next source of improvement.

The current best is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.7131 accuracy. The image modality contributes meaningfully in the multimodal setting (~0.06 gain over RNA-only transformer multiprofile at 0.6530), yet the image-only ResNet50 baseline was very weak (0.2079), suggesting the image encoder quality may be a bottleneck. Config_039 makes a single clean change—swapping ResNet50 for the stronger ViT-L image encoder—while keeping all other settings at their best-known values (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion). This isolates the effect of image encoder quality on multimodal fusion performance. It is the best use of this experiment because it exploits the strongest identified direction (weighted multimodal fusion) with a logical, single-variable extension that has the highest expected upside, and if it succeeds, the remaining 2 experiments can further refine around the new best.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 > pca_n2000, multiprofile > singleprofile, transformer ≥ avgpool, weighted > concat, and imagenet_vit_l > resnet50. However, the scgpt RNA encoder has never been tested in any multimodal or multiprofile setting. Config_051 isolates the effect of RNA encoder (scgpt vs scvi_n200) while holding all other components at their empirically best settings. This is the highest-value remaining question: if scgpt matches or exceeds scvi_n200, it opens a new direction for the final experiment; if it underperforms, it confirms scvi_n200 as optimal and solidifies our confidence in config_039 as the final answer. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, testing the single unexplored encoder in the proven-best architecture is the most informative use of the slot.

The best result so far is config_039 (scVI n200 + ViT-L + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250). The evidence strongly supports scVI n200 over scGPT/PCA, ViT-L over ResNet50, multi-profile over single, and weighted over concat (0.7131 vs 0.6878 with ResNet50). However, the weighted-vs-concat comparison was only tested with ResNet50; ViT-L produces fundamentally different feature geometry (patch-based, higher-dimensional), so the optimal fusion strategy may shift. config_038 isolates this single variable (concat vs weighted) while keeping all other components at their best-evidenced settings. As the final experiment, it either reveals a new best configuration or confirms that weighted fusion is robust across image encoders, solidifying config_039 as the definitive winner.
